subject: Post-cutover: intermittent egress failures and MTU/ICMP translation issues
messages:
From: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearfield-health.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Matt Harris <matt.harris@acme-networking.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-cutover: intermittent egress failures & partial payload truncation

Hi Priya,

We completed the private deployment cutover to Redwood's VPC yesterday evening. Since then we've seen intermittent failures when our clients upload larger artifacts (~>1.2MB) to S3 via the private egress.

Symptoms:
- Uploads fail with 200 OK but truncated objects (hash mismatch) or keep retrying.
- TCP retransmits and RSTs visible from some hosts, but not consistent across all clients.
- tracetcp/traceroute shows an apparent PMTU/fragmentation-related issue: ICMP "fragmentation needed" responses are not reliably making it back.

Attached is a short excerpt from our transfer logs and a tcpdump snippet captured at our app host (not the gateway): clearfield_transfer_log.txt (attached).

Can you triage? This is causing production errors across a handful of customers.

Thanks,
Michael Torres
Network Ops Lead
ClearField Health

Attachments: clearfield_transfer_log.txt

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearfield-health.com>, Matt Harris <matt.harris@acme-networking.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-cutover: intermittent egress failures & partial payload truncation

Michael — thanks for the quick signal and the logs. We're on it.

Initial plan:
1) Priyom/Vanessa/Karthik: triage egress path from Redwood edge -> transit -> ClearField. Please provide:
   - edge routing table snapshot and active SNAT entries
   - conntrack summary for affected time window
   - tcpdump on the egress interface (if possible) capturing ICMP type 3 code 4 and MSS values
2) Michael: can you provide a traceroute from an affected host to the S3 endpoint (UDP ICMP and TCP) and confirm whether any intermediate firewall/ACL changes were made by your transit provider during the cutover?

If this is PMTU related, short-term mitigation options are:
- allow ICMP type 3 code 4 (fragmentation needed) return path through any middleboxes, or
- apply an MSS clamp on the egress NAT to avoid fragmented packets.

I'll coordinate with the team and update within 2 hours.

— Priya Natarajan
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference

Attachments: acknowledgement-template.txt

From: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearfield-health.com>, Matt Harris <matt.harris@acme-networking.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-cutover: intermittent egress failures & partial payload truncation

Quick findings from the edge:
- edge-routes-20260518.txt and conntrack-brief.txt attached.
- We see asymmetric return path for traffic to S3 IP ranges: outbound via Redwood edge -> TransitA, return via TransitB (policy-based routing at provider).
- conntrack shows SNAT port reuse spikes and some established sessions being torn with RST after ~30s which correlates with the failed uploads.
- tcpdump (we captured a small sample; will upload full pcap if you want) shows repeated "ICMP frag needed" from a mid-link but the ICMP replies have source addresses that do not match the expected next-hop, and our transit provider is dropping them due to an ACL mismatch.

Temporary mitigations tested (non-disruptive):
- Enabled conservative MSS clamp on a single egress node (1200 bytes) — immediate reduction in failures for the test host.
- Adding an explicit ALLOW for ICMP type 3 code 4 on the candidate security group allowed some ICMP back, but not all — provider path still drops some.

Recommendation:
1) Short-term: keep MSS clamp on for affected egress pool and request transit provider to permit ICMP frag-needed back to our edge IPs.
2) Mid-term: coordinate route symmetry with TransitA/TransitB or announce a more-specific to avoid asymmetric return.
3) Follow-up: full packet capture from edge -> transit to provide to ClearField and Acme for deeper analysis (I can drop tcpdump to shared Drive).

Priyom Das
Network Reliability Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: edge-routes-20260518.txt, conntrack-brief.txt, tcpdump_edge.pcap (available on request)

From: Matt Harris <matt.harris@acme-networking.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Cc: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearfield-health.com>
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-cutover: intermittent egress failures & partial payload truncation

Thanks team — Acme looked into the path at the provider level. Observations:
- We are seeing PMTU discovery failing because intermediate firewall boxes are producing "fragmentation needed" but those ICMP messages are being dropped on the return due to an ACL that only allows established TCP/UDP flows (no ICMP).
- The ICMP that is generated uses an address that the return ACL does not expect because of asymmetric transit selection.

Immediate actions we recommend (low risk):
- Add ACL to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 back to the Redwood edge IP CIDR for the affected transit leg. Example rule: permit icmp any <edge-cidr> type 3 code 4.
- If transit ACL changes are slow, keep the MSS clamp applied at Redwood egress as a stop-gap and then remove once ACLs are in place and PMTU validated.

We can push the ACL change in the next maintenance window (ETA 2 hours) if you give us the exact edge prefixes to permit.

Matt Harris
Field Engineer, Acme Networking Services

From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Torres <michael.torres@clearfield-health.com>, Matt Harris <matt.harris@acme-networking.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 15:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-cutover: intermittent egress failures & partial payload truncation — remediation and next steps

Update for ClearField + Acme:

What we did:
- Applied a targeted MSS clamp (1200) on the affected egress pool at 02:10 UTC on 2026-05-19.
- Requested and validated an ACL change on TransitB to allow ICMP type 3 code 4 back to our edge prefix (TransitB applied change at ~08:30 UTC).
- Temporarily opened a security-group exception for ICMP to assist validation during the window; this has been scoped to the ClearField test CIDR and will be removed after verification.

Results:
- Over a 24-hour verification window uploads that previously failed are now succeeding and hash/size mismatches have stopped for the sampled customers.
- No broad impact to unrelated flows observed.

Follow-up actions (owner / ETA):
- Karthik: create a runbook for this class of PMTU asymmetry (JIRA-ENG-4412) — due 2026-05-26.
- Priyom: produce full packet captures and a concise report for ClearField + Acme (shared Drive link above) — due 2026-05-20.
- Priya: schedule retrospective with ClearField to discuss permanent options (announce a more-specific, transit rebalancing, or keep managed MSS profiles) — tentatively 2026-05-22.

I'll keep the temporary MSS clamp in place for 48 hours and coordinate removal after we confirm no regression. Please ping me immediately if you see any new failures.

Thanks all for the rapid collaboration — Michael, appreciate the clear logs you sent; Matt, appreciate the ACL help.

— Priya Natarajan
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
